about.text: Leyden, from Dutch: Leidse kaas, is a semi-hard, cumin and caraway seed flavoured cheese made in the Netherlands from cow's milk. It is made both in factories and on farms, historically in the Leiden area.

sources.text: The first paragraph of its article, shortened.
The photograph, its author and its licence, from its page.

how.label: add cumin
how.text: Leyden is made from partly skimmed milk with cumin seed worked into the curd, while plain curd on the flat faces keeps the seeds out of the rind. The rind is coloured red with annatto and stamped with Leiden's crossed keys.

sources.text: The table, the facts and the words on how it is made, from these.

steps.name: add cumin
steps.note: About 75 g per 100 L of milk, with plain curd kept for the white bottoms.
